- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true price if sentiment is stable.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome (especially in first 5–7 days), reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 7–10 days, especially if sentiment is weak.
- If sentiment is strongly negative and price is falling, model often underestimates drop — add 1–3% buffer to forecast to account for volatility.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, use 20-day EWMA instead of 30-day average to avoid overfitting to recent noise.
